title.zh: Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 5 将椭圆曲线运算量子电路门数削减约 17 倍
title.en: Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 Cuts Quantum Circuit Gate Count for Elliptic-Curve O

current_state.zh:
10 月 16 日，Anthropic 发布研究称，Claude Mythos 5 在一个自动化评估系统的辅助下，自主重新设计了八个量子电路，覆盖量子化学、优化、物理模拟与数论领域，并称这些新设计优于此前已发表的方法。其中，一个椭圆曲线点加法电路使用的量子门数量减少约 17 倍，但所需量子比特增加 12%；用于优化算法 DQI 的 Reed–Solomon 解码电路门数则减少约 12 倍。

Anthropic 称这些重新设计的电路优于此前已发表的方案，而椭圆曲线点加法的结果关系到评估量子攻击椭圆曲线密码所需的资源规模。该工作目前仍停留在电路设计与验证阶段。

Claude 提出了一种可逆的模逆算法，无需存储分支历史，取代了步骤数量和顺序依赖输入的扩展欧几里得方法。这些结果尚未在真实的量子硬件上验证。
current_state.en: Anthropic research shows Claude Mythos 5, aided by an automated evaluation system, autonomously redesigned eight quantum circuits and produced a reversible modular inversion algorithm that cuts an elliptic-curve point-addition circuit's gate count roughly 17x (with 12% more qubits) and trims DQI Reed–Solomon decoding gates ~12x, though results remain unverified on real quantum hardware.

updates.background_zh: Decoded Quantum Interferometry（DQI）是一种量子算法，通过把线性可满足性问题归约为对量子态叠加进行有界距离解码，来近似求解组合优化问题，其中 Reed–Solomon 解码是最昂贵的环节。点加法是求解椭圆曲线离散对数的量子电路中的原子运算，而模逆运算则是这类电路中资源开销最大的组件之一。
updates.background_en: Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) is a quantum algorithm for approximating solutions to combinatorial optimization problems by reducing instances of linear satisfiability to bounded-distance decoding over superpositions of quantum states; the Reed–Solomon decoding step is its most expensive component. Point addition is the atomic operation in quantum circuits for elliptic-curve discrete logarithms, and modular inversion is among the most resource-consuming components of those circuits.
updates.market_impact_zh: 传导路径是间接且长期的：更廉价的椭圆曲线点加法电路会影响对量子攻击椭圆曲线签名方案所需资源的估算，这一风险叙事涉及比特币、以太坊等资产；但目前这仍是未经硬件验证的电路设计结果，不会改变近期任何托管、流动性或协议参数。
updates.market_impact_en: The transmission path is indirect and long-horizon: cheaper elliptic-curve point-addition circuits feed into resource estimates for quantum attacks on elliptic-curve signature schemes, a risk narrative that touches assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, but this remains a circuit-design result without hardware validation and does not change any near-term custody, liquidity or protocol parameter.
